main.why: The most frequent verb in any text; carries identity, location and 'there is'.
Every text negates; placement before the verb is the reading cue.
The question job in reading; direct speech and dialogues in simple texts turn on it.
The 'can' job; irregular, built on sum, so unreadable without being taught.

main.job: relative 'who / which / that' linking a clause to a noun
main.why: Relative clauses appear in almost every sentence of connected prose.

main.job: 'and' attached to the end of the second word
main.why: Very frequent and invisible to beginners, who read it as part of the word.
Place where is everywhere in narrative; the case after 'in' changes the meaning.
Main contrast connector in simple prose.
Speech verbs frame reported speech throughout narrative texts.

spares.why: The other job of 'in'; motion is as frequent as place in narrative.
Frequent in both questions and narrative.

jobs_covered.existence: sum, esse (est / sunt = there is / are)
jobs_covered.people reference: verb endings mark person; no pronoun set started

shape.notes: Reading slice: no greetings or conversation phrases. Pronoun set (ego, tū, nōs, vōs) and question-particle triad (-ne, nōnne, num) deliberately not started: both would need more slots than a 10-term list can spare, and verb endings carry person. Verbs cited as first person present + infinitive.
